name: Funk ceramics
region: San Francisco Bay Area and Davis, California
summary: Hand-built ceramic sculpture from California that turns toilets, typewriters, self-portraits and bad taste into loud, crude and funny figures. Bright low-fire glazes and drips keep the clay rude.

philosophy.core_thesis: Clay is a rude, funny material, so a sculptor can make a toilet, a typewriter or a bust of himself and treat high art as a joke.
design_principles: Build the figure by hand with coils and slabs, and leave the thumb and the tool marks.
Take the subject from daily life or from the artist's own face: a toilet, a typewriter, a pet, a bust.
Make the form lumpy, thick and a little wrong, with a big head and small hands.
Cover the clay with loud low-fire glazes and overglaze china paints, in hot pink, yellow and green.
Let the glaze run, drip and pool, and leave blisters and pinholes.
Add a joke in the title or in a small detail: a text, a pun or a crude word on the base.
Make the piece 30 to 120 cm tall, as a single piece or a small group on a plain base.
Fire the piece in several runs, and add paint and glaze in layers until the surface is rich.
anti_patterns: A thin, symmetrical vase in a quiet glaze
A polished, factory-smooth surface with no tool marks
A refined classical pose in white biscuit
A pretty pastel pattern in a floral print
A serious, solemn tone with no joke
A copy of an old master in porcelain

form.shape: Hand-built objects and figures: a toilet, a typewriter, a bust, a head with a tongue, a dog, a bottle, a hand with a cigarette.
form.profile: A lumpy, thick outline with a big head, small hands and a slumped body; the form leans, sags and bulges.
form.foot_and_rim: A thick, flat or uneven base that rests on a slab, or a plain block of clay; edges are rough and torn, with no turned foot.
form.proportion: Height 30 to 120 cm; the wall is 10 to 25 mm thick, and the head is about a third of the height for a bust.
rules: Build by hand and leave the thumb marks.
Pick a daily subject or a self-portrait.
Distort the form: swell the head, shrink the hands.
Use loud, mixed glaze and overglaze colours.
Put a joke in the title or the detail.

bodies.rule: Use a grogged stoneware or earthenware that stands up when it is hand-built in a large size. Keep the surface rough, and keep fine porcelain out.

methods: assemblage of cast and found parts
forming.joins: Parts are scored, wetted and pressed together by hand. Cracks and joins are left open and show as part of the form.
forming.details: Thumb and tool marks, cracks at the joins, drips of glaze on the base, and small words or numbers cut into the clay.

glaze.pattern: Glaze in pools and drips of hot pink, yellow and green, with a china-paint line and sometimes a decal or a text. Parts of the clay stay bare.
glaze.gloss: Gloss and satin, 40 to 95 GU; blistered and bubbled areas break the light.
glaze.wear: The low-fire glaze chips at the edges and crazes in a net. The overglaze colours are bright at first and rub with handling.

palette.strategy: Loud, clashing hot colours on a rough clay: hot pink, lemon yellow, acid green and turquoise, with black and a patch of bare clay.

firing.kiln: A university or studio electric kiln, with a biscuit firing, a low-fire glaze run and a china-paint run.
processes: repeat runs for layers of colour
firing.scale: A single artist in a studio or a university ceramics department, with one-off pieces and small series of a few figures.
firing.signs: Thumb marks, drips and blisters of glaze, cracks at the joins and the signature or title cut into the base.

pieces.form: A typewriter with keys as fingers, in glazed stoneware, a joke of the studio
Self-portrait head with a tongue, a thick neck and a drip of glaze
A glazed toilet with a lid and a text on the bowl, in bright pink
Man and dog on a block, with a loud yellow glaze and a black outline
A big bulldog with a heavy jaw, a blistered green glaze and bare feet

positive: loud low-fire glaze in hot pink and yellow
glazed toilet or typewriter as sculpture

evidence.title: Bust of George Moscone by Robert Arneson

emotion.target_response: A rude laugh: the viewer sees a toilet or a face in loud glaze, and feels free to treat art, and clay, with no respect.

use_cases: a gallery label for funk sculpture
a prompt for a loud, funny ceramic figure
a brief for a studio ceramic with a joke
avoid_when: the brief wants a refined, elegant tableware piece
the brief needs a delicate porcelain figure
the brief wants a quiet, craft-tradition vessel

modifiers.how: Change to a thrown and altered earthenware form, use engobe drawing and a white glaze, and cut the loud colours.
Change to a mould-pressed earthenware figure with a lead glaze and flat enamel colours, and make the form symmetrical.
